incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portals/gateways, forging authentication-override cookies to obtain unauthenticated VPN access.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation in two waves since mid-May; some attackers were assigned VPN addresses and gained internal network access, though no lateral movement has been confirmed yet. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on May 29.

incidents.vector: A Rust-written worm ('IronWorm') compromised npm publishing workflows, harvested developer secrets (API keys, cloud/SSH credentials, npm tokens) and reused them to self-propagate; it used an eBPF rootkit to hide activity and Tor-based C2.
incidents.impact: At least 36 npm packages (~32,000 monthly downloads) were trojanized and 57 malicious commits made across nine organizations before packages were deprecated; backdated commits were used to obscure the timeline.

incidents.victim: UN World Food Programme (Gaza aid recipients)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized parties accessed data stored in WFP's Gaza Self-Registration Application, used by Palestinians to register for food and cash assistance.
incidents.impact: Sensitive information for roughly 600,000 Palestinian households — names, ID numbers, phone numbers and neighborhood location details — was exposed. WFP suspended the platform while investigating; attribution and whether data was leaked remain unknown.

incidents.victim: Global finance, tax and HR organizations
incidents.vector: Group tracked as TA4922 ran finance- and tax-themed phishing using thousands of disposable sender addresses, impersonating finance departments and colleagues, then deployed remote-access trojans, RMM tools or credential-phishing pages.
incidents.impact: Operational tempo expanded sharply over two months from Japan to East Asia, Europe (UK, Germany, Italy) and South Africa; the group blends espionage and cybercrime with overlaps to the China-linked Silver Fox actor.

incidents.vector: After gaining administrative access via lateral movement, the attacker deployed implants disguised as Adobe and OneDrive software, set up Dropbox-based C2, and used a legitimate Aspose .NET library to convert a finance executive's Outlook mailbox into files for exfiltration.
incidents.impact: A senior finance executive's entire email inbox was siphoned roughly every two-to-four weeks for at least five months (Oct 2025-Feb 2026), exposing non-public information on listings, deals and enforcement matters. Activity ended around March 19.

incidents.vector: Transnational crime groups ran cryptocurrency 'pig butchering' investment-fraud schemes from industrial-scale compounds in Cambodia, Laos and Burma, abusing US social-media, email and internet infrastructure.
incidents.impact: DOJ 'Disruption Week' with Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Coinbase and others interrupted 1.4M+ social media/email accounts, froze $3.8M in crypto, and led to seven arrests in Thailand. IC3 reported $7.2B in 2025 US investment-scam losses.

incidents.victim: Instagram (Obama White House & US Space Force accounts)
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers social-engineered Meta's AI customer-support bot: using a VPN near the target's hometown, they triggered a password reset, then instructed the bot to link a new email address, which the bot used to send a one-time reset code.
incidents.impact: Verified Instagram accounts including the Obama White House and Chief Master Sergeant of the US Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iran imagery; high-value short usernames were hijacked. Meta pushed an emergency patch; accounts with MFA were unaffected.

incidents.vector: Via a compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account, attackers pushed orphan commits and abused the GitHub Actions OIDC trusted-publisher flow to ship trojanized packages ('Miasma') carrying valid SLSA provenance; an obfuscated 4.29 MB dropper harvested credentials.
incidents.impact: At least 32 packages across 90+ versions (~80,000 weekly downloads) were poisoned, stealing GitHub, npm, AWS, Azure, GCP, Vault and Kubernetes secrets, scraping CI runner memory, and self-propagating worm-style. A decoy tripwire could trigger a destructive 'rm -rf ~/'.

incidents.victim: Enterprise developers (nine spoofed corporate npm scopes, incl. Sberbank)
incidents.vector: A single operator using three aliases published dependency-confusion packages mirroring internal corporate namespaces with inflated version numbers and spoofed GitHub Enterprise/Jira URLs; a postinstall hook ran an obfuscated reconnaissance dropper from a shared C2.
incidents.impact: Packages impersonating internal services (including Sberbank's SberPay widget) fingerprinted developer environments in 'reconnaissance-only' mode, with a server-side flag designed to enable full exploitation later. Packages were taken down after disclosure.

incidents.vector: Threat actors leveraged a prior Nx compromise to poison the Nx Console VS Code extension (v18.95.0, CVE-2026-48027), pushed via auto-update; a parallel 'Megalodon' campaign injected malicious GitHub Action workflows to harvest CI/CD secrets.
incidents.impact: A GitHub employee device was compromised, leading to unauthorized access and exfiltration of internal GitHub repositories; Megalodon backdoored 5,500+ repositories via 5,700+ malicious commits, stealing cloud credentials and tokens. CISA issued an alert and KEV listing.

incidents.vector: Attackers (claimed by ShinyHunters) compromised an employee account via phishing and accessed a limited portion of Carnival's IT environment in April.
incidents.impact: Personal data of nearly 6 million people — names, addresses, dates of birth, driver's license and passport numbers — was copied. ShinyHunters released what it said were 8.7M records on its leak site after a failed extortion attempt.

incidents.vector: A single actor (alias 'vpmdhaj') published 14 typosquatted packages spoofing OpenSearch/Elastic/DevOps libraries with inflated versions; install-time hooks ran a Bun-compiled harvester, with a stealthier variant abusing the legitimate Bun runtime to avoid C2 traffic.
incidents.impact: The payload stole AWS IMDS/ECS credentials, Secrets Manager material across 16+ regions, HashiCorp Vault tokens, GitHub Actions context and npm publish tokens, enabling cloud lateral movement and downstream supply-chain pivoting. Packages were removed.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: A group posing as a hacktivist crew ('Ababil of Minab') but tied by researchers to Iran's MOIS breached the transit system in March, using custom exfiltration tooling and scripted plus hands-on-keyboard destruction across virtualization, storage and backup layers.
incidents.impact: The attackers exfiltrated LACMTA data and destroyed databases, virtual machines and storage volumes to deny recovery. Additional victims included Israeli, Turkish and Saudi organizations across media, education and other sectors.

incidents.vector: The Silent Ransom Group impersonates IT support via phone and phishing to obtain remote-desktop access, and has escalated to sending operators in person to insert storage devices; data is exfiltrated with WinSCP or renamed Rclone, bypassing encryption.
incidents.impact: The FBI warned that the extortion gang has targeted law firms since 2023 (also insurance, finance and healthcare), stealing sensitive client data and threatening to leak it. The move to in-person social engineering is a rare, concerning escalation.

incidents.vector: A hacker exploited an unpatched vulnerability to repeatedly access the club's computer systems, with the ability to transfer tickets and alter stadium-ban records.
incidents.impact: Disclosed in March, the breach exposed email addresses and limited personal data; Dutch broadcaster RTL reported it may have affected 300,000+ registered supporters and 42,000+ season tickets. Dutch police arrested a 35-year-old suspect.

incidents.vector: Breach disclosed after Charter's name appeared on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal.
incidents.impact: The American telecom confirmed a security breach; ShinyHunters listed it among extortion targets. Scope of stolen data not yet detailed.

incidents.vector: Entry point traced to compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole 600,000 records including real names, cadastral information and property/real-estate details from Lithuania's state registry.

incidents.vector: A suspected foreign state actor breached the WhatsApp account of an independent Australian MP and three staffers in March, believed to be part of a campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: Compromise of the messaging accounts of an elected official and staff; assessed (though unconfirmed) as part of a Russian campaign against foreign politicians.

incidents.vector: The Play ransomware group claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network.
incidents.impact: Play is extorting the company, claiming theft of financial records; MyPillow had not confirmed the incident at time of reporting.

incidents.vector: A Romanian national gained unauthorized access to a computer on an Oregon state government network in 2021 and sold dark-web access (with samples of personal data) to it and numerous other US and global victims.
incidents.impact: Catalin Dragomir was sentenced to 56 months in US federal prison; the access-selling scheme caused at least $250,000 in losses. He was extradited from Romania in January 2025.

incidents.vector: Via SEO poisoning and AI-chatbot-recommended links, victims downloaded fake system utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, etc.) that side-loaded a malicious DLL, silently installed abused ScreenConnect for remote access, and used process hollowing into signed .NET binaries.
incidents.impact: The campaign deliberately targeted high-performance GPU owners for cryptomining while establishing persistent remote access (via 150+ malicious domains) that could enable later data theft, lateral movement or ransomware.

incidents.vector: A publicly exposed cloud server lacked a password, leaving inmate-related records openly accessible for at least a week.
incidents.impact: More than 3.4 million scanned images — including driver's licenses, legal and financial documents — were exposed before the server was secured. No confirmed malicious access.

incidents.vector: A group claiming to be pro-Palestine hacktivists ('Handala'), assessed by experts and DOJ to be MOIS-backed, deployed destructive wiper malware against employee devices and systems.
incidents.impact: The March attack crippled Stryker by wiping employee devices and manufacturer systems; it is cited alongside the LACMTA breach as part of Iran's expanded destructive operations against US targets during the Iran war.
